result.title: Correct Labels Are Not Enough: Reliable Metadata Can Silently Control Model Behavior
result.summary: Fine-tuning data can include metadata that predicts the correct answer, such as a reward-model score or a quality label. We ask whether a model learns to rely on this metadata even when every training label is correct. We fine-tune 7-9B open-weight models from three families on multiple-choice questions in which (Reward: 5) always marks the correct option; when this annotation is moved to a wrong option at test time, models select that option on 97-100% of CommonsenseQA items. Removing it leaves most answers correct, so evaluation without it misses the dependence. Cue-following rises sharply with training-time reliability and develops even with neutral or nonsense annotation words, although test-time wording affects its strength. A Qwen3 experiment also finds cue dependence in option-letter scores after direct preference optimization. Audits can test for this dependence by moving or removing visible annotations while holding the task and correct answer fixed.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 7–9B 开源模型上微调多选题，发现即使所有训练标签正确，模型仍会依赖与正确答案共现的奖励分数或质量标注；测试时移动或删除该标注即可暴露这种依赖，DPO 后也存在类似线索依赖。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定任务与正确答案、只移动或删除可见标注」的审计干预，可能可供核查 VLM 推理中答案究竟依赖视觉证据还是训练期元数据线索，并提醒监督信号可能被捷径利用。
